name: Cartography of the Unwired Self
creator: Dr. Yelena Murakami-Sow
description: A dense philosophical work arguing that BCI integration has not merely augmented human cognition but has fundamentally restructured the phenomenology of selfhood — that the 'unwired self' is not a nostalgic ideal but a theoretical construct that never existed, and that identity has always been a collaborative, networked process. Murakami-Sow draws on pre-Collapse philosophy of mind, Yoruba concepts of personhood, and contemporary neuroscience to propose a new framework she calls 'distributed interiority.' Published through a Tier 3 academic press in physical hardcover with a simultaneous licensed neural-feed edition.
medium: physical hardcover and licensed neural-feed academic channel
cultural_impact: Widely taught in Tier 3-4 university programs and cited extensively in legal arguments around BCI personhood, synthetic consciousness rights, and corponation data-ownership cases. It gave intellectual vocabulary to movements that had previously struggled to articulate their positions.
controversy: Heavily criticized by The Unclocked collective, who argue the book provides philosophical cover for mandatory BCI integration by suggesting the unwired self is incoherent. Murakami-Sow has repeatedly denied this reading but the debate remains unresolved and sometimes hostile.
story_hooks: A chapter Murakami-Sow excised before publication — arguing that corponation-owned BCI infrastructure makes 'distributed interiority' a form of corporate colonization of the self �� has been leaked and is circulating on pirate channels.
A synthetic consciousness cites the book in a formal legal petition for personhood, and Murakami-Sow is subpoenaed to testify about whether her framework applies to non-biological minds.
Someone is annotating physical copies in libraries with handwritten rebuttals in at least four languages, and the annotations are becoming as widely discussed as the original text.
